issue_context.title: The result is not as expected when using the hint of use_index_merge
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

[1.txt](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/files/5754106/1.txt)
download the file
```
use test;
source "path of the file";
SELECT /*+ use_index_merge(t1)*/ COUNT(*) FROM t1 WHERE (key4=42 AND key6 IS NOT NULL) OR (key1=4 AND key3=6); 
```
<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
31
### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
0
### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)
release-5.0-rc
<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

review_comments: Actually we can use IndexMerge for this case, as long as we keep the whole filter `(key1=1 and key2=2) or (key1=4 and key3=6)` in the selection, that should be the original intention of https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/20425.
